title: Running Containers
subtitle: Master docker run flags — environment variables, port mapping, restart policies, resource limits

content.text: The full docker run flag toolkit

content.code:
docker run \
  -d \
  --name my-api \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -e DATABASE_URL="postgres://localhost/mydb" \
  -e NODE_ENV=production \
  --env-file .env \
  -v /data/uploads:/app/uploads \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --memory 512m \
  --cpus 1.0 \
  myapi:1.4

# Flag breakdown:
# -d                      run in background (detached)
# --name my-api           give the container a name
# -p 3000:3000            host:container port mapping
# -e KEY=value            set an environment variable
# --env-file .env         load all vars from a .env file
# -v /host/path:/c/path   mount a host directory as a volume
# --restart unless-stopped restart automatically (except manual stop)
# --memory 512m           cap RAM at 512 MB
# --cpus 1.0              limit to 1 CPU core

# ❌ Never bake secrets into an image:
# ENV DATABASE_PASSWORD=mysecret  ← visible in docker history, image layers

# ✅ Pass secrets at runtime:
docker run -e DATABASE_URL="postgres://user:pass@db:5432/myapp" myapi

# ✅ Even better — use an .env file:
# .env file contents:
# DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@db:5432/myapp
# REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
# JWT_SECRET=supersecret123

docker run --env-file .env myapi

# ✅ Best for teams — Docker secrets or external secret managers:
# (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, GitHub Actions secrets)

items: no (default) — never restart. Use for one-off containers.
always — always restart, even after docker daemon restarts. Use for critical services.
unless-stopped — restart always, except when manually stopped. Best for most production services.
on-failure[:max-retries] — restart only on non-zero exit code. Good for job containers.

content.code:
# Production web server — should always be up
docker run -d --restart unless-stopped -p 80:80 nginx

# Database — restart on crash, max 5 times
docker run -d --restart on-failure:5 postgres:16

# One-off data migration script — don't restart
docker run --restart no my-migration-script

# Check restart policy of a running container
docker inspect my-api --format '{{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}}'

# States: created → running → paused | stopped | exited

# Created (not started)
docker create --name my-app -p 3000:3000 myapi

# Start
docker start my-app

# Pause (freeze all processes — RAM preserved)
docker pause my-app
docker unpause my-app

# Stop gracefully (SIGTERM → 10s grace → SIGKILL)
docker stop my-app
docker stop --time 30 my-app   # extend grace period to 30s

# Force kill immediately
docker kill my-app

# Remove (must be stopped first)
docker rm my-app
docker rm -f my-app   # force: stop + remove in one

questions.question: A container runs a web server that sometimes crashes. You want it to auto-restart, but stop if you manually docker stop it. Which restart policy?
questions.explanation: 'unless-stopped' restarts the container automatically on crash or daemon restart, but respects a manual 'docker stop'. 'always' would restart even after a manual stop. 'on-failure' only restarts on non-zero exit, which misses crashes that exit cleanly. 'unless-stopped' is the right default for long-running services.

faq.q: How do I see the resource usage of all running containers?
faq.a: docker stats — shows a live, htop-style view of CPU%, MEM USAGE, NET I/O, and BLOCK I/O for all running containers. Add a container name to watch just one: docker stats my-api. Add --no-stream for a one-shot snapshot.

examples: --memory and --cpus are essential in shared servers — without limits, one runaway container can starve all others
docker run --env-file .env is the standard pattern for 12-factor apps — config comes from the environment, never from the image
